answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit bids, with rewards released only after counterparties confirm delivery. A disputed job triggers review by randomly selected, stake-bearing peers; proven fraud burns the offender's stake and excludes it from future selection. A summit contract might fund glacier sensors while an onyx supplier earns only after verified data arrives. Sybils can multiply accounts, but each needs capital and each failed identity risks forfeiture.
